text:
marina: Heads-up — brought Ivy-9B (int4) into canary this morning. Observing a 15-25% tail-latency regression vs. baseline on p99 for short-chat traces :thinking_face:

sanjay: saw that too. p95 mostly fine, p99 spikes when requests hit cold KV cache and when batch size > 4.

lucas: can you paste the traces? curious if it's kernel scheduling or extra memcpy.

marina: pasted a snippet from the worker logs: 
```
[2026-03-21T08:12:03Z] worker-3 | infer_request id=abc123 seq=42 batch=6 max_new_tokens=64
[2026-03-21T08:12:03Z] worker-3 | kv_cache_miss key=0x7f8a evict_check=0.0 alloc_retry=1
[2026-03-21T08:12:03Z] worker-3 | memcpy 24ms | compute 18ms | total 98ms p99
[2026-03-21T08:12:03Z] worker-3 | OOM fallback triggered, reclaimed 120MB
```

marta: interesting — OOM fallback shows up even though resident memory steady. Might be fragmentation. Are we still using aggressive prefetch for Ivy?

marina: yes default prefetch=on for int4 models during canary. I toggled prefetch=off in one microslice and p99 dropped by ~10ms.

sanjay: that suggests prefetch + batching interacts poorly for this model's chunking. For Ivy the kv shard size is slightly larger and prefetch may allocate contiguous buffers that fragment.

lucas: can we try two quick configs and run a 1h smoke: (A) prefetch=off + batch_max=4 + max_new_tokens_default=64, (B) prefetch=on + batch_max=3 + small_slot_reserve=64MB?

marina: creating canary routes now. deploy-bot: canary deploy initiated for route ivy-int4-canary-20260321.

deploy-bot: 1/3 nodes updated -> 2/3 nodes updated -> canary running.

marta: also add a kv_eviction_threshold tweak: lower threshold to 0.6 for A, 0.7 for B. That may reduce transient evictions.

sanjay: good call. I'll prepare the config diff.

sanjay: config snippet for A:
```
model: ivy-9b-int4
prefetch: false
batching:
  max_batch: 4
  prefer_small_batches: true
max_new_tokens_default: 64
kv:
  eviction_threshold: 0.60
  slot_reserve_mb: 128
```

sanjay: config snippet for B:
```
model: ivy-9b-int4
prefetch: true
batching:
  max_batch: 3
max_new_tokens_default: 64
kv:
  eviction_threshold: 0.70
  slot_reserve_mb: 64
```

lucas: timeline — run both configs for 1h each on identical traffic replay (prod-sampled). Capture p50/p95/p99, tail OOM counts, and quantization-quality checks (BLEU-ish prompt QA).

marina: started A on node group alpha at 08:45, traffic replay attached.

marta: I'm seeing fewer OOM fallbacks on A already. p99 improved ~12ms for short-chat traces, long-form sees no change.

marina: logging a small regression in a few eval prompts — answers occasionally drop a token early when max_new_tokens set to 64 vs 128 baseline. Could be exposure bias from quantization + shorter max gen.

sanjay: let's add an eval hook to run the standard QA set with gold references and measure EM/F1 before deciding final defaults. We don't want to degrade quality for latency wins.

lucas: agreed. Also let's add a small warmup path: on cold start raise slot_reserve_mb for 30s to reduce first-request fragmentation, then step down.

marina: noted. I'll implement warmup: slot_reserve_mb=256 for 30s.

deploy-bot: A run complete (1h). Metrics summary uploaded to /replay/runs/ivy/20260321/A_summary.json

marta: A results — p99 down 9-14ms, OOM fallbacks reduced by 70%, but qa_em dropped 0.8% (stat sig).

marina: starting B now on group beta.

deploy-bot: B run complete (1h). Metrics summary at /replay/runs/ivy/20260321/B_summary.json

lucas: B results — p99 down 5-8ms, OOM fallbacks reduced 45%, qa_em unchanged. So B is safer quality-wise but smaller latency wins.

sanjay: decision time: A gives better latency and memory stability but small QA hit. Could be tuned (increase max_new_tokens_default back to 96) to recover quality.

marina: propose staged rollout: adopt B as default canary route for now (safer), and run an A-variant with max_new_tokens_default=96 + prefetch=false for a longer eval (24h) with targeted QA set. If QA holds, merge A-variant as optimized profile.

marta: +1. Also add a kernel scheduling note for runtime team — Ivy int4 shows higher memcpy spikes; may be a vectorized-copy path issue.

lucas: I'll open a ticket with perf traces and attach the run artifacts. Ticket: RI-2026-ivy-int4-kmem-copy-investigation.

marina: thanks all. I'll update the model catalog entry with the canary profile and the recommended defaults: batch_max=3, prefetch=on (safer), kv_eviction=0.7, max_new_tokens_default=64, and link to the follow-up A-variant evaluation. :white_check_mark:

marta: ping me if the 24h run shows QA drift and we'll rollback.

sanjay: great work. we'll reconvene after 24h. :eyes:
